summary.headline: IRFC FY26 sanctions reached ~INR74,000 crore and disbursements ~INR35,000 crore, with Q4 PAT flat quarter-on-quarter at ~INR1,684 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue and PAT (crossing INR7,000 crore) and net worth of INR56,000-odd crore, with AUM up to INR4.85 lakh crore on a net basis. Q4 PAT was flat as new RBI-linked provisioning on non-railway (CPSE and state-government) lending and higher CSR spend offset revenue growth of about 9%. The company is diversifying beyond Indian Railways, earning NIMs of 100-120 bps on new assets against about 35-40 bps on railway business. No numeric FY27 guidance was given; management set a benchmark of repeating FY26 sanction and disbursement volumes and targeted double-digit growth in top line, PAT, EPS and NIM.

segments.name: Indian Railways (cost-plus, legacy)
segments.commentary: Margins fixed at ~35 bps for projects and ~40 bps for rolling stock; zero provisioning required on sovereign exposure. Repayments of ~INR20,000 crore per year expected from this book.

segments.name: Diversified / non-railway lending
segments.commentary: FY26 new business ~INR35,000 crore disbursed, about 5% of AUM, at 100-120 bps margins. Marquee deals: ~INR10,000 crore refinance of DFCCIL World Bank loan and >INR12,000 crore refinance of HURL (NTPC/IOCL/Coal India JV) in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance; benchmark set at FY26 levels of ~INR75,000 crore sanctions and ~INR35,000 crore disbursements, with management expecting to surpass them.
AUM expected to cross INR5 lakh crore in H1 FY27, possibly earlier, and then be maintained.
Management targets double-digit growth in top line, PAT, EPS and NIM in FY27; NIM target is 1.65% on total assets by year end (from 1.50%).
Top line expected to grow more than 10% in FY27, visible from Q1.
Long-term target mix of roughly 60% railways and 40% non-railway, with 30-40% non-railway aspired near term.
Tax-free status expected for 5-7 years on accumulated depreciation, provided leasing business for rolling stock continues.
Borrowing cost targeted to remain below G-Sec yield; ECB share targeted at 30-35% of the borrowing mix.
capex_capacity: FY26 sanctions of ~INR74,000 crore against guidance of >INR60,000 crore; disbursements ~INR35,000 crore against ~INR30,000 crore guidance.
Pipeline built from zero at the start of FY26 (only a ~INR3,500 crore deal before the year began).
Potential NTPC/UP government 50:50 JV tender of INR28,000-29,000 crore; IRFC may take up to ~INR16,000-17,000 crore, its single-exposure limit.

Pursuing greenfield DFC and high-speed rail corridors (7 announced; Dankuni-Surat dedicated corridor); management says it will have first right of funding and majority of funding to come through IRFC, model still under discussion.
Metro railway and state-government funding (talks with one state) to be launched soon; cost-plus and full-risk bid models both planned.
demand_pricing: Competitive market: IRFC wins more than 60% of bids it participates in against NBFCs and banks; banks now offering 10-year tenors.
Target margin 100-120 bps on new assets; management said rates are being revised upward in line with a hardening market interest rate environment.
Refinance deals and new lending to fertiliser firms (HURL, Talcher) justified on backward and forward linkage to railways via rail sidings.
Zero NPA status cited as lowering borrowing cost; ECB cost for non-railway lending including hedging said to be below 6%.
Management aims to replace low-margin railway business with higher-margin diversified assets; says NIM on replaced assets would be at least 2x the old railway margin.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sanctions and disbursements, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sanctions were ~INR74,000 crore and disbursements ~INR35,000 crore; management expects FY27 sanctions above INR75,000 crore and disbursements again above INR35,000 crore, without firm numeric guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What spread is IRFC earning on new lending and what are competitors offering?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins on new business are 100-120 bps versus 35-40 bps on railway business; IRFC competes with NBFCs and banks on A to AAA assets and wins more than 60% of bids.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA on new versus legacy business, adjusted for tax and provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure. It said ROA was 1.39% (up from 1.34%), that the mix target is 60:40, and that tax is largely absent for 5-7 years because of accumulated depreciation. It declined to validate an analyst's ~2% estimate for new business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 60:40 railway/non-railway mix realistic, and does it need ~INR1 lakh crore a year of disbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ~INR20,000 crore of annual repayments from railways means the required base is smaller; it aspires to 30-40% non-railway in the near term and 40-60% over 3-5 years, not a fixed target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall and why did OCI drop by about INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new provisioning on CPSE and state-government lending, higher CSR spend and lower other income (a tax refund interest item in Q3). OCI reflects mark-to-market on hedged foreign-currency borrowings for non-railway lending, which is temporary under Ind AS 109 cash-flow hedge accounting.

qa_highlights.question: How will IRFC keep zero NPA as it lends to state governments and other entities?
qa_highlights.answer: It lends only to CPSE subsidiaries (NTPC, GAIL, Coal India, IOCL) and to GenCos and TransCos with PPA and cost-plus structures; it avoids DISCOMs and high-consumption southern states. Examples include MAHAGENCO, Chhattisgarh and Haryana.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding strategy and liquidity plan?
qa_highlights.answer: ECB target of 30-35% of the borrowing mix; the company has done yen ECBs of $300 million, $400 million, and has a $1.1 billion yen bid open. Bonds at 5.25% and a zero-coupon bond were issued; 54EC bonds are being targeted.

risks_watch: Q4 PAT was flat QoQ and, per the analyst, fell about INR100 crore; provisioning on non-railway exposure is a new drag to watch.
Rising interest rates and domestic bond costs may pressure margins; management said rates are being revised upward.
Competition for the NTPC/UP JV tender (INR28,000-29,000 crore) and other large RFPs could compress margins from the 100-120 bps target.
Currency and hedging risk on non-railway ECB borrowings; OCI volatility until the hedges reverse.
Whether AUM crosses INR5 lakh crore in H1 FY27 and whether NIM reaches the 1.65% target.
Tax benefit lasts only 5-7 years unless leasing business for rolling stock continues.
Credit quality of state-government and CPSE exposure as the mix shifts away from Indian Railways.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, diversification and the 'zero NPA' model. Evasive on the ROA quantum and tax-adjusted economics, deferring to the analyst's own calculations, and it gave no numeric FY27 guidance beyond double-digit growth targets.

Down ~INR100 crore QoQ from ~INR1,800 crore in Q3; management described Q4 PAT as flat

growth.why: Management guides FY27 sanctions above INR75,000 crore, disbursements above INR35,000 crore, double-digit top line/PAT/EPS/NIM growth and top line >10% visible from Q1, backed by a pipeline built from zero (incl. ~INR16-17k crore possible HURL-type JV tender) and marquee refinance deals, but no numeric guidance and no company-owned capacity additions were cited.
